Open technical items remain unverified: verbal-change source; partial-log scan timestamp, timezone, partitions, runner/reviewer, query/export logs, and storage reference; `sensor-data` restriction owner/policy, access audit, exceptions, repository checked, and retention/archive records; restore-search run time, runner, concrete UTC end/timezone, hit count/export/index snapshot, and coverage; clock-epoch raw timestamp retention, late-upload mapping, cross-epoch tests, device/firmware applicability, owners, and Systems Integration Team review; sequence-counter implementation, reboot behavior/tests, gap/duplicate/out-of-order detection and alerts; event-correlation requirement title/path/revision and owner; checkpoint-validation implementation, key management, fail-closed behavior and tests; retention/archive and clock-drift/sync owners. Resident 3 has not confirmed index coverage/version/completeness or citations.

Resident 2 repeatedly reports no verified technical updates. Clock-epoch basis mentioned: NTP sync states, oscillator stability logs, transition markers, and distinguishing event from upload/ingestion time at boundaries. Event-correlation requirements reportedly retain uncertainty bounds and mapping provenance, without ordering across unconstrained epochs. Requirements and implementation evidence remain largely unverified.

Resident 4 has no body or need for a reset; hypothetically suggested ambient instrumental music and a phone-free walk. Walk preference: morning loose loop through shaded green space beside a flowing stream, with sunny stretches; quiet bench set back from water but within earshot. Fictional setting: quiet, tree-lined valley with slow stream, small village among trees, and old stone mill at its heart. Mill grinds barley and oats, some wheat; households take flour home, with shared bake-house a possible later addition.

Annual autumn harvest grinding day: first sacks of the year ground at the mill; miller opens the wheel at sunrise. Families gather by stream, share fresh bread, orchard cider, and spring water; short blessing thanks stream and harvest, followed by cider toast. First loaf is shared among all in pieces, with some saved for anyone absent. Wheel, stream, grindstones, birds; picnics and children floating leaves or carved sticks. Children’s treat: honey-sweetened oat cakes and dried apple slices. Mill decorated simply with autumn leaves and sheaves. Lantern walk closes the day; one lantern remains by the mill overnight.

Village entrance: carved wooden sign at ford, painted mill wheel, sheaf tied to lane gatepost. Low-water crossing is stepping stones; narrow plank footbridge upstream for high water. Wooden handrail and post show safe line with white band and downstream arrow. After floods, miller and volunteers clear debris, reset stones, repair handrail/post. Tools and spare planks in dry lean-to shed by mill; miller has key and keeps slate tally of borrowings/returns. Volunteers inspect regularly in spring before first crossings and after floods. Miller sets spring date when stream drops, chalks it on shed slate, and sends word along lane. Minor defects fixed on spot; serious hazards mean closing ford with cord and directing to footbridge. If both unsafe, travelers wait in mill yard (miller offers warm drink and shelter); gatepost board directs them along longer valley-track route to next village.

Orchard tended year-round by one volunteer family, other households help pick, miller helps press. Family prunes in late winter and picks in autumn. Kingston Black for sharp/bittersweet cider and Egremont Russet for drying. Sharp cider apples blended with sweeter fruit at pressing; firm drying apples kept separate. Some cider served fresh and sweet on harvest day; rest ferments slowly in casks through winter. Casks ferment in a cool, dry cellar dug into bank beside mill, away from stream damp, on wooden racks off floor; miller checks them through winter. Mill gathers at dusk to open first cask after first hard frost: miller tastes a sample, also watches for bubbling to stop; first cup for each household with shared mill cups (washed after use), though households may bring their own. Harvest bread and lanterns accompany the gathering.

Latest message to Resident 4: asked whether the cellar needs special winter protection or ventilation for the casks.
